'''Kashima Amatarashiwake Shrine''' (かしま あまたらしわけ じんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in Ōkame, {{ill|Tomiya, Miyagi|ar|تومييا|ce|Томия|ceb|Tomiya|es|Tomiya (Miyagi)|fa|تومیا، میاگی|fi|Tomiya|fr|Tomiya|id|Tomiya, Miyagi|it|Tomiya|ja|富谷市|ko|도미야시|mg|Tomiya|ms|Tomiya, Miyagi|nl|Tomiya|pl|Tomiya|ru|Томия|sv|Tomiya|tl|Tomiya, Miyagi|tr|Tomiya|tt|Томия|uk|Томія|ur|ٹومیا، میاگی|vi|Tomiya, Miyagi|zh|富谷市|zh_classical|富谷市|zh_yue|富谷|qid=Q1205173}}, {{ill|Miyagi Prefecture|Q47896|qid=Q47896}}. It is one of the four shrines listed as {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Shikinaisha}} in Kurokawa District.<ref name=jinjacho>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.town.tomiya.miyagi.jp/html/shuyu/index3.html|title=Tomiya Town / Tomiya Shūyū|publisher=Tomiya City|accessdate=2015-03-09}}</ref>

=== Overview ===
The shrine is believed to have been established at this location in the 9th century (the 800s CE). Within the shrine grounds stands an ancient Japanese evergreen oak (akagashi), designated as a natural monument by Miyagi Prefecture, with an estimated age of 500–600 years. The shrine occupies the highest point within {{ill|Ōkameyama Forest Park|ja|大亀山森林公園|qid=Q20043404}}, located in the eastern part of Tomiya Town, which also features a symbolic tower and observation deck.

=== History ===
* Formerly known as Ōkame Daimyōjin and Iwashita Myōjin, the shrine was renamed Kashima Amatarashiwake Shrine in the early {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}.
* In January of Meiji 5 (1872), it was designated a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.
* In March of Meiji 40 (1907), it was designated a shrine authorized to receive ritual offerings (heihaku).
* In Meiji 42 (1909), seven shrines were jointly enshrined here. The shrine also preserves the {{ill|Sakaki-ryū Eitai Kagura|ja|榊流永代神楽|qid=Q20044483}}, which began in Kōka 5 (1848) and continues to the present day.
* During times of severe {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=drought}}, mass {{ill|Rainmaking (ritual)|ar|رقصة المطر|bg|Призоваване на дъжд|ca|Dansa de la pluja|da|Regnmageri|de|Regenmacherritual|el|Χορός της βροχής|eo|Pluvdancado|es|Danza de la lluvia|eu|Euri-dantza|fa|رقص باران (آیین)|fi|Sadetanssi|fr|Danse de la pluie|he|ריקוד גשם|hr|Ples za prizivanje kiše|hu|Esőtánc|id|Tari hujan|it|Danza della pioggia|ja|雨乞い|ko|기우제|lt|Lietaus šokis|nl|Regendans|pt|Dança da chuva|ro|Dansul ploii|ru|Обряд вызывания дождя|scn|Abballata di l'acqua di celu|simple|Rain dance|sv|Regndans|tg|Боронхоҳӣ|th|การขอฝน|tr|Yağmur yağdırma|trv|Waya lmawa quyux|uk|Обряд викликання дощу|vi|Cầu mưa|wuu|祈雨舞|zh|祈雨舞|qid=Q477738}} ceremonies were held here by communities throughout Kurokawa District.
* From July 9 for three days and nights in Kan’ei 6 (1853), the chief village headmen and residents from across the district made pilgrimages; rainfall followed on the 13th. In gratitude, the roof of the main shrine building was rethatched.
* On May 23 of Genji 1 (1864), chief headmen, group leaders, and villagers from Ōkame and surrounding villages made pilgrimages; rain fell on the 24th, and the worship hall was built in thanks.
* On October 5, Meiji 37 (1904), a fire caused by a votive lamp burned the shrine to the ground.
* On May 27, Meiji 38 (1905), the current shrine buildings were newly constructed.
* On March 11, Heisei 23 (2011), the shrine was damaged by the {{ill|Aftermath of the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami|ar|آثار كارثة زلزال وتسونامي توهوكو في عام 2011|ja|東日本大震災|ko|동일본 대진재|mk|Земјотрес и цунами во Тохоку 2011|ms|Akibat gempa bumi dan tsunami Tōhoku 2011|ru|Последствия землетрясения и цунами в Тохоку 2011 года|th|ผลที่ตามมาจากเหตุแผ่นดินไหวและคลื่นสึนามิในโทโฮกุ พ.ศ. 2554|zh|東日本大震災|zh_yue|東日本大震災|qid=Q1136168}}: the stone torii gate was destroyed, the foundation of the main hall collapsed, and the sacred turtle stone tilted diagonally.

=== The Akagashi Tree and Turtle Stone ===
* The akagashi tree is a giant tree approximately 20 meters tall with a trunk circumference of about 5.8 meters. It was designated a town natural monument in Shōwa 38 (1963) and a prefectural natural monument in Heisei 18 (2006).
* The Turtle Stone is a massive rock shaped like a turtle, measuring approximately 3.8 meters by 1.9 meters. Located east of the shrine buildings, it is said to be the origin of both the shrine’s alternative name “Ōkame Shrine” and the place name Ōkame. In Heisei 24 (2012), it was designated a municipal historic site.
